comparison: Compared to empf-v5 (which passed both model_ae_gan_multimodal and precision_gaussian_fp32 under exact polar_factor SVD but hit the 900s wall-time cap on five_word_joint_smoke), empf-v6 resolved five_word_joint_smoke throughput (549.7s) while confirming the study competing explanation that unthresholded 32-iteration Newton-Schulz drifts on small ill-conditioned MLP layers (hidden <= 64).
conclusion: empf-v6 cleared five_word_joint_smoke in 549.7s (20,001/20,001 steps, modes=5, quality_fraction=1.0, mass_tv=0.0189) and passed 11/13 counted Tier 1 gates, but applying 32-iteration cubic Newton-Schulz to small dense matrices (hidden <= 64) regressed model_ae_gan_multimodal (reconstruction_mse 0.0405 vs 0.0080) and precision_gaussian_fp32 (step 834 cdf_ks 0.0509 vs <= 0.05).

decision_outcomes.reuse_note: Compatible original receipts; overlapping readouts are not independent runs or additive costs

hypothesis: Replacing serial 2D cuSOLVER SVD calls with DualNorm's guarded cubic Newton-Schulz regularized polar profile (optimizer_dense_profile = 'newton_schulz_v1') eliminates multi-agent GPU cuSOLVER contention on five_word_joint_smoke so empf-v6 clears all 13/13 counted Tier 1 gates within wall-time budgets and advances through Tier 2/3 to realize gaussian1d_stability, target_shift_recovery, ring_hold, and ring_extension gains.
next_action: Define empf-v7 with a size-gated hybrid dense profile (newton_schulz_hybrid_v1) mirroring DualNorm's per-offset convolution rule: exact rank-1 normalization for vector-shaped 2D heads, exact polar_factor SVD for small matrices (min_dim < 64 or max_dim < 128), and guarded cubic Newton-Schulz for large dense matrices (min_dim >= 64 and max_dim >= 128).

study.competing_explanation: If bounded 32-iteration cubic Newton-Schulz dense polar updates introduce drift relative to exact cuSOLVER SVD on ill-conditioned 1D or discrete-simplex MLPs despite 1e-3 orthogonality and input-relation guards, empf-v6 will regress five_word_joint_smoke, gaussian1d_stability, or precision_gaussian_fp32.
